title: Good Pixel Art AI platform?
author: Shot-Abies-7822
selftext:
Hey! 

Game dev + pixel artist here. Whilst I still do 99% of my assets by hand, I'd love to see if there are any *good* AI pixel art platforms out there, or how some of you have incorporated pixel art AI generators into your workflow? 

I used Pixellab AI, but I found the quality very, very inconsistent and poor. It was decent for a quick brainstorm session, but the output felt very...soulless and just too clean & perfect, which is the defies the whole point of pixel art, I think.



Anyways, would love to hear your experiences with pixel art AI platforms.

comments.author: woodysixer
comments.body: Try spritecook.ai – it’s been pretty impressive when I’ve used it via MCP with Claude Code.

comments.author: NovaGuarda
comments.body: The real answer is no. No matter what tool people try to sell you, AI generation is just too inconsistent. If someone would have an answer, they'd be rich. As it stands, pixel lab is sota.

replies.author: Mental-Frosting-7752
replies.body: i just told codex 5.6 sol ultra what i wanted 8 dir animation walking and attacking and it looks perfect (in my eyes) and had codex clean it up with aseprite. Works perfect for me

replies.author: QueenSavara
replies.body: But are those Perfect animations true pixels ir again a mess like usual?

replies.author: Shot-Abies-7822
replies.body: You can give codex/claude access to asperite?

replies.author: Phllori
replies.body: Yeah, it's useful for prototypes, but since you seem to know what you're doing, that shouldn't be a problem.

replies.author: sloth2121
replies.body:
Guy above says ai generation is too inconsistent.   
It’s more so somebody can’t create a generative system thats going to understand the standard Youre looking for. 

Yes plenty of gen ai has issues but if you can hook into a mcp and have your ai do it, it opens the doors to create a standard, “For this project I have these 3 reference pieces (or more). I want you to analyze them and see everything they have.   
Building: made out of bricks, with a dirty mossy stone texture, random spots where bricks are missing, tombstones some are broken, dig spots from freshly dug graves, etc… 

Your ai then creates things that match the level of other items you already have.

replies.author: RevenueChemical6910
replies.body: what was your prompt like? I've had a difficult time getting good AI art. Can you share any samples you have and what you prompted to get them? Would love to see!

replies.author: cxfoulke
replies.body:
And Its probably gonna be no for a long time. Especially if your pixel art style is lower resolution I.e isnt taking a base image gen and then pixel art filter over the top. 

There just isn't a lot of context for pixel art animations and complexity of categorisation for pixel art in low resolution is really high. 

I wouldn't be surprised If pixel art animation is a final frontier for ai art models. 

I've tried pixel art lab alot and it's a decade away from being actually viable for unsupervised/ unedited game ready assets.

3d topology seems like a far more "solveable" problem.

comments.author: ratridero
comments.body:
Finding AI-generated pixel art that doesn’t need some manual cleanup is still difficult... I’ve been developing my own Godot plugin, Adoto, which brings Codex and a Pixel Art Studio directly into the editor. It can currently generate and revise pixel-art assets, use existing sprites as character or style references, clean up generated images, adjust palettes, slice sprite sheets, create animations and TileSets, and add the finished assets directly to a Godot scene. The results aren’t always consistent (yet), and the plugin is still faaar from perfect, but it’s already possible to go from an idea to a usable in-game asset without leaving Godot. It’s starting to become something genuinely interesting... but again, this is super early.. also exploring a combination with TRELLIS + Blender for 3D generation and rigging.

replies.body: cool stuff man! thanks for sharing

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: The best bet would be training your own lora (Krea 2 probably) on your specific pixel art assets that you've made and then setting up automatic processing on what it spits out to deal with any mixels and palletize the colors more deterministically than an AI model could ever currently do).

comments.author: CleverAdvisorPrime
comments.body: I found the best was using an AI tool online to make the sprite and animate it. Then have Codex/ChatGPT clean it up.

comments.author: Count_Triple
comments.body:
It's not very difficult to set up a pixel art or sprite pipeline within ComfyUI. I asked Google ai how and just followed the steps.   
We can add nodes that use an image model and/or weighted reference images. We can control the pixel count and color palette of the output images.

I need this pipeline because I have about 700 different 32x32 sprites to make. I can generate a base version for each and edit them all
